Stage 2 / Make every investigation count

Which claim can change the repair?

Not calculated

FalkorDB solves two hypothetical branches per evaluated claim: reject it in the conservative graph, or confirm it in the lower-bound graph. Neither branch changes the evidence. Rank the possible cost effect, then investigate the actual source.

Calculate a plan to see certified cost sensitivity. Ordinary page refreshes do not run extra counterfactual solves.
How to read the ranking

Rejection saving is the possible drop in conservative cost if this one claim is rejected. Confirmation uplift is the possible increase in the confirmed-only lower bound if it is confirmed. The score is the larger effect divided by declared method-effort units, an uncalibrated proxy—not a probability, token estimate or financial value. An unavailable source cannot be invented.

Finite equal bounds prove the conservative repair remains cost-optimal under every resolution of the captured unknowns. A zero single-edge score or a partial scan proves neither independence nor irrelevance: several uncertainties can matter together. Equal-cost alternative repairs and split balance are outside this stopping guarantee.

Controlled example: five records with declared costs and inspectable evidence. Loading it replaces the active run, not its saved files.

Stage 3 / Evidence-bound context

What the investigators remember

No stored memories

Verified investigation receipts become episodic, semantic, and procedural graph memories. Each note is checked against current evidence when recalled. Procedures only suggest methods; they never establish new verdicts. The model cannot author trusted evidence through this panel.

Investigate a candidate to record memory.

Current verified memory summaries appear here on request.

Stage 4 / Shared investigation tasks

Two specialists, one evidence graph

No tasks

The code-evidence and provenance investigators claim exclusive, expiring tasks in FalkorDB. Unresolved code findings are handed to provenance without copying verdicts. Failed claims can be safely retried; evidence is replayed after restart.

Start a coordinated run to observe claimed work and handoffs.

How the decision works

Evidence becomes a repair.

Each confirmed edge says that a training example and an evaluation example cannot both remain in this candidate release. HOLDOUT uses a weighted bipartite vertex cover, reduced to minimum cut, to choose exclusions with the lowest declared cost.

Two conflict policies

Answer-leakage separation requires bounded answer evidence; whole-file identity alone does not prove answer relevance. Exact-record separation only prohibits identical complete contents and does not promise to catch renamed answers. Choose the rule at import, independently of exclusion-cost weights.

Why there are two bounds

The lower bound uses confirmed conflicts. The upper bound also treats every unresolved candidate relationship as a conflict. Investigation can close that gap. The guarantee applies to the compiled relationships and policy, not every possible undiscovered source of contamination.

What the agent does

The agent chooses investigations, follows source provenance, and records evidence. The optimizer computes the repair. A recorded replay displays captured results; it does not execute an agent or FalkorDB in your browser.

Use your local backend

Serve this interface from the HOLDOUT backend, then reload. Live controls become available when /api/state responds. See the project README for setup and start commands.
